verdict.tagline: Hilarious physics battles with endless custom creation tools.
for_you_if: you enjoy setting up chaotic physics battles
you want to design custom units and factions
you like tackling challenging tactical campaigns
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance during massive battles
you tire quickly of the core gameplay loop

distortion_flags.sentence: Approval rises sharply after the opening hours as players move beyond initial impressions.

cohorts.summary: Early players find the battles grow repetitive quickly before discovering deeper tools.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that battles become repetitive or stale quickly, leading to boredom within a short play time.

citations.review_text: It's what it says is, and yet I expected something more. I got bored too quickly to recommend it.

I do not understand why everybody loves this game so much. The pvp/pve gets stale after like 20 minutes, and each battle is a gamble. I would forgive this game if it at the very least TOLD YOU WHAT THE UNITS DO. I genuinely don't know what half the units I have do, because, as far as I'm aware, there is no way to view it in game before you deploy the troops into battle. So yeah, it's a terribly overhyped game. I rest my case.

It's really boring, every level is the same, overwhelm the AI with as many enemies as you can afford and that's it, if it doesn't work (which is often) then try, try again, its fun for about 10 minutes.

single_points.text: One reviewer states that there is no way to view what units do in the game before deploying them into battle.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the extensive custom content creation and direct unit control, though huge fights demand robust hardware.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that completing all levels without losing is required for 100 percent achievement completion, which they describe as challenging.

citations.review_text:
I love cartoony graphics and low poly graphics, and seeing them mixed with such vibrant colors just work perfectly for this goofy adventure of a game. 

The gameplay is fun and never predictable, the many different variations of units is the reason why people play this for so many hours on end. I think what really makes this game so much fun, is the mechanic to take over a unit and control it, I cant tell you how much time I've spent as units instead of looking over. It also just makes it a lot more fun to play, since you can really make an impact on the current battle with your bright human wits. 

If your a completionist, then yes I do recommend it, but this game does take prefections since you have to complete all levels in the game without losing once.... And yes that really sucked, but in the process of doing it, I did really start enjoying it, and I think you would too, especially if you dont mind tougher games to 100%. 
So difficulty wise I would say its a 6.5/10 and the game takes around 28-34 hrs to 100%.
TABS is for: Totally Agonizing Score Completionist

I don't have anything bad to say anything about this game other than the fact that the battle outcomes can be random sometimes but maybe it was meant to be that way, i dont know.

You can recreate some of history's famous or infamous battles or create entirely new battles,make any and all types of units and factions imaginable, and recreate some of the most famous battlegrounds or even your own, the possibilites are nearly endless.

This is my first actual review on a game. TABS was a game I first discovered a few years ago and I loved it. The hilarious ragdoll characters, the secret units, the custom content, it was possibly my favourite game ever. So now I feel very sad after hearing that Landfall has ended the development of TABS. I know that the game is a decade old now,  but hearing this really disheartened me.

If you're reading this as a person that wants to play a funny, simulation game with infinite community content you should buy this game.

citations.review_text: It is fun  when i put random units togher to fight sometime there not smart and there is also very cool mods for this and its 3D i like it it also a campain and sanbox mode.

if you love God Simulators, buy this! Totally Accurate Battle Simulator is a Battle Simulator (duh) where you spawn units on a red and blue team, and watch them go NUTS on eachother! Theres a campaign, and a variety of maps, units, alongside Multiplayer, multiple factions, and custom content, make nonsensical maps or overpowered units, I have over 300 hours playing it, and those 300 hours were worth it.

For the gameplay, there are 3 main ways to play. There's Sandbox, in which you have infinite resources and are able to modify both of the teams. This is the main way to play. You can mess around with the troops provided, create epic battles, and answer questions that philosophers have debated for years like: "Who would win in a fight: 20 raptors or 60 medieval soldiers?" or "Would 2 tanks be enough to stop 6 mammoths?". It's awesome.There's also Campaign, where you need to destroy a team of enemies using the troops at your disposal and a designated budget. Then there's Online, in which you can share the fun with random strangers across the world.The gameplay is an 8/10. You can also control units, which is pretty fun. And the most fun feature of them all: Custom content. You can make any troop or map you want! Ever wondered who would win: Drake or Satoru Gojo in WW1 trenches? Well, now you can, using the custom troops and custom maps editor! There's not much to say about optimization, like a 5/10. The game is mainly for the shits and giggles, really entertaining. If you like sandboxes, strategy games, funny random games, and like to mess around, get it. If you prefer challenging games with story and don't like sandbox or strategy, don't. Super fun and sometimes pretty satisfying battles, with a bunch of freedom and creativity. I've played some of the campaigns, and they can be fairly hard, but still mostly fun. The sandbox is where the best battles lie, and you can definitely sink hours into just those. However, by far the best feature of this game is the custom unit creator. The possibilities are huge with the unit creator, and beyond that you can create maps, battles, campaigns, and factions, and then share them on the workshop. The workshop is filled with super creative and fun units and battles, and these custom aspects are where the majority of my hours in this game have gone. Definitely recommend if you're a fan of any battle sims, just know that this one is not to be taken too terribly seriously, though once you embrace the goofiness it's tons of fun.
